question: Does training on 63 rivers instead of 12 give better forecasts for the same 12 rivers, and for rivers never seen?
outcome: Given training on 63 rivers instead of 12, median NSE 1 day ahead for the same 12 rivers goes from 0.59 to 0.60 (onsets warned 19% to 17%); for rivers never seen, from 0.22 to 0.38 with basin properties (0.31 to 0.43 without them; 50 training rivers instead of 11); the verdict is NOT YET.
outcome_caveat: With the river gauge, 1 day ahead (lowest to highest single training in brackets): median NSE 0.590 (0.542 to 0.598) with the 12 rivers in training, 0.604 (0.581 to 0.597) with 63; onsets warned 18.7% (18.0% to 18.5%) against 17.3% (16.7% to 17.0%), false warnings among the onset warnings 59% and 50%: no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 10 of 12 rivers, p = 0.016) and clear loss for the onsets warned. Without the gauge: NSE 0.443 (0.355 to 0.434) against 0.453 (0.411 to 0.427), onsets warned 17.2% against 18.0%: no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 7 of 12 rivers, p = 0.151) and no clear difference for the onsets warned. The 63-river models ran 1733 updates on average against 1233 for the 12-river controls (best at 1133 against 633), that is 576 against 1689 training sequences per river at the best update: at equal updates each river gets about a fifth of the training. The equal-training arm (lstm63eq_wq: 5x the updates and patience window) was not run in this pass, so this comparison cannot yet tell 'more rivers do not help' from 'each river got a fifth of the training'. Rivers never seen (weather only), 1 day ahead: median NSE 0.216 with basin properties and 0.313 without when 11 rivers were in training (05_lobo.py, one training per river), 0.376 (0.343 to 0.377) and 0.434 (0.408 to 0.432) with 50 (three seeds); a river in training scores 0.443 with the 12-river model and 0.453 with the 63-river model. Against the leave-one-out models: clear gain with properties and clear gain without (NSE; every 50-river seed above the single leave-one-out training: yes and yes). The 50 lie closer to the 12 than the 11 did: the nearest training gauge is a median of 39 km away against 110 km, the nearest training basin in property space 1.42 against 2.23; so part of any difference is proximity, not the number of rivers, and one model scores all 12 rivers (its seed noise is shared by all of them).

notes: Quoting. The sentence in `outcome` is accurate arithmetic but incomplete as a statement of the result: any document (report, README, slides, Q&A, guide) must quote `outcome_full` (the outcome plus `outcome_caveat`), never `outcome` alone. Both are computed from the tables of this file.

Design (a). lstm63_wq and lstm63_w are one LSTM each, trained on the 63 south-eastern CAMELS basins with a complete record (the 12 study basins and the 51 others of results/basin_audit.csv; flood.candidate_ids(), checked when loaded: a row for every day of 1980-10-01 to 2014-09-30, no missing value, all ten properties present: data_checks). Network, inputs, settings (results/lstm_all.json, key config) and seeds are those of the stored controls lstm_wq and lstm_w; the only change is the list of training rivers. Scalers (weather, flow, the ten properties) and loss weights come from the training years of the training rivers. The networks are scored on the 12 only and the saved prediction sets hold the 12 (flood.evaluate, the same thresholds, the same test years as every set of the report); the 12 inside the 63-basin tables are bit-identical to the stored 12-basin tables (data_checks).

Stopping. flood.fit is unchanged: at every check it scores the validation years (2000-2005) of ALL its training rivers and stops on their mean NSE over rivers and leads. With 63 rivers that mean includes the 12, so the stopping point is chosen on the validation years of 63 rivers, not of the 12 (and of the 50, never the 12, for the never-seen models). stopping.*.validation_nse_of_the_12_at_that_update gives the 12's own validation score at the chosen update, information only: nothing was chosen on it; for the stored 12-river controls it equals the trainer's own best_val_nse (checked).

Training per river. Each update draws 32 sequences of one river each, uniformly over the training rivers, so with 63 rivers a river gets about a fifth of the sequences per update. The 12-river controls ran 1233 updates on average (best at 633): 1689 sequences per river at the best update; the 63-river models ran 1733 (best at 1133): 576 sequences per river, 0.34 times the control's. 0 of 3 lstm63_wq trainings and 0 of 3 lstm63_w trainings reached the update limit of 2000 before the stopping rule was met (controls: 0 of 3 and 0 of 3). The 'equal training per basin' arm (lstm63eq_wq: 5x the update limit and the patience window) was not run in this pass.

Design (b). unseen50_w_static and unseen50_w_nostatic: past weather only (a river without a gauge has no flow input), trained on the 50 other rivers - the 51 minus 03471500, which lies inside 03473000 (S F Holston River near Damascus): the outlines show 198 km2, 100% of 03471500 and 25% of 03473000's basin, so for that river the 51-river design would not be a river never seen; no other pair of the 12 x 12 and 12 x 51 outlines shares any area (0 others found). Scalers, loss weights and the stopping point come from the 50 rivers only (the validation years of the 50); one model forecasts all 12; the high-flow level of each of the 12 (observed 95th percentile of its training years) is used for scoring only, as in 05_lobo.py. The 12's flow is never read in training (leak_probes.training_ignores_the_12). Same settings as lstm_w, three seeds per variant (05_lobo.py had one training per river).

Comparability with 05_lobo.py is limited, in this order. (1) Proximity: the nearest training gauge is a median of 39.3 km from the 12 here and 110.1 km in the leave-one-out test (8 against 4 of the 12 have a training gauge within 50 km); the nearest training basin in the ten-property space the model sees is 1.42 against 2.23 (5 against 7 of the 12 have a property outside the training range). Neighbouring rivers share storms and geology, so 'never seen' here means 'no flow record of this river', not 'far from any gauged river'. (2) One model scores all 12 here against twelve different models in 05, so the seed noise is shared by all 12 scores and the 12 scores are not independent draws. (3) The 50 are 22 northern lowland, 18 southern lowland and 11 mountain basins (the 11 of 05 were balanced); Hyco Creek, NC and Myakka, FL have a larger share of days without any flow (5.2% and 0.6%) than any of the 50 (largest 0.4%), so they are rivers of a kind the 50 do not hold. (4) Budget and stopping: 05 capped its trainings at 1000 updates and patience 4, one seed; here 2000 / 6, three seeds. A comparison of one 05 training with the average of three seeds favours the seed average a little: unseen50_*_s<k> and the single-seed rows of the rule are given for that reason.

Choices made on the 12. Hidden size and learning rate were chosen in 04_lstm_all.py on the validation years of all 12 rivers (a weak leak for the never-seen test: 04 found the candidates equal within seed noise, as 05_lobo.py states). Three of the ten properties (p_mean, aridity, p_seasonality) are CAMELS climate averages of 1989-2009, which overlap the validation years and four test years; no property is computed from the flow record.

Warnings. The scores of the gauge sets use the observed high-flow level (flood.evaluate, trigger 1.0), as every other score of the report. A river without a gauge has no such level, so for the never-seen sets unseen.sets.<name>.own_level gives the warnings at the model's own level (the 95th percentile of its own training-years forecasts for that river: the rule of 05_lobo.py, reproduced here and checked against its stored numbers); the verdicts in verdicts use the observed level.

Test years. The test years were scored once, after every training had finished; the trainings printed validation scores only. The sets, seeds, settings, stopping rule and comparison pairs were fixed before any test score was computed. The weight of any single comparison is small: Wilcoxon p describes 12 neighbouring, dependent rivers and is not corrected for the many comparisons made; with 12 rivers the smallest p is 0.0005.

Timing. The laptop was shared with other jobs (mean 1-minute load average at the validation checks of these trainings: 6.3); every training ran under flood.cpu_lock (0 s of waiting in this pass). training seconds therefore describe this machine on this day, not the cost of a training.

Prediction sets: lstm63_wq, lstm63_w, unseen50_w_static, unseen50_w_nostatic (seed averages) and one per seed (_s<k>); each holds the 12 study rivers only. Networks: results/models/<set>_s<k>.pt, plain dicts that torch.load(weights_only=True) reads (weights, settings, scalers including the properties', the training rivers in training order, the property values, the split, the training record); reload_check rebuilds each from its file alone.

Controls: lstm_wq and lstm_w (seed averages; their single seeds _s0 to _s2) of 04_lstm_all.py, and lobo_w_static, lobo_w_nostatic, lobo_ref_w_nostatic, lobo_rf_w of 05_lobo.py, were read from their prediction files and re-scored with the code used for the new sets; checks_against_stored_results shows they reproduce the numbers their own scripts stored (largest difference 0.0e+00).
0 values in this file are not numbers (NaN: shares whose denominator is zero, or a p-value that is not defined); they are written as null (strict JSON). A reader must treat null as 'no value'.
what_was_not_done: The equal-training arm (lstm63eq_wq: 5x the updates and 5x the patience window, with the gauge, three seeds) was left out of this pass (--no-equal) because the laptop was too busy for its three long trainings: 'python code/17_more_basins.py --extend' trains them and rewrites this file and the figure with the arm included.
Not independently checked: the work order requires a second agent to recompute the headline numbers from results/preds with its own code; none has done so for this script.
13_uncertainty.py (test years and rivers drawn again) is not extended to the new sets; the seed ranges and the checks of gain_rule are all this file holds.

No 63-river model without basin properties (lstm63n_w): the in-training partner of unseen50_w_nostatic is the 12-river lobo_ref_w_nostatic, so that comparison changes the training set (12 -> 63 rivers) as well as the 12's presence.

No simple-model yardstick (ridge, random forest) trained on 63 or 50 rivers: only the stored leave-one-out forest lobo_rf_w (11 training rivers) is shown for scale; this experiment changes the training set, not the input.

No dose-response (random subsets of the 50) and no buffered leave-out (the 51 minus every river within 100 km of the one held out), which would separate 'more rivers' from 'closer rivers'; only the split of the 12 by distance (unseen.by_distance) and the rank correlations.
No more than 63 rivers: the 516 CAMELS basins with a complete flow record, and the gap handling the trainer would need for the others, are not tried (ROADMAP.md, step 3).
Hidden size and learning rate were not tuned again for the larger training set; the 'equal training per basin' arm is the only change of budget and was run with the gauge only.
No report subsection, no row in the key figure, no update of PLAN.md or README.md (NEXT_STEPS_FOR_AGENTS.md, sections 3 and 6): documents must quote outcome_full, not outcome alone.
make_handin_zip.sh was not changed: its 'full' archive packs data/derived, which now also holds the 63-basin cache (about 50 MB).
